summary: Intermittent p99 spike and 504s from continuous-batcher idle-threshold drift under low-burst workloads
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports intermittent high tail latency (p95->p99) and occasional 504 gateway timeouts on text generation endpoints. Problem appears during low-burst workloads (short bursts of small requests) and began after the serving-runtime 2026-03-03 rollout.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing requests returned 504s and saw p99 latency > 2.5s (baseline ~250ms).
- Affects production traffic for LexiDocs dedicated capacity in us-east.
- Business impact: user-facing timeouts for document previews in product.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexidocs-dedicated-us-east
- Serving runtime version: 2026.3.03-canary (rolled to prod 2026-03-03)
- Autoscaler: configured reserved + burst policy

Steps to reproduce (synthetic):
1) From a client in us-east, send bursts of 10 concurrent small-completion requests (max_tokens=64) at 1 QPS sustained for 5 minutes, with random inter-burst idle intervals of 10-30s.
2) Observe p95/p99 and error rates on the route.

Observed behavior:
- p50/p75 stable; p95 shows periodic bumps and p99 spikes to 2-3s every ~20-40s.
- Gateway logs show internal timeouts and downstream "504 read timeout" entries correlated with serving-runtime worker queue wait exceeding 1.5s.
- Continuous-batcher metrics report increases in "idle_wait_ms" and a growing "pending_batch_window" metric right before spikes.

Expected behavior:
- Small bursts should batch quickly with max_wait ~10-30ms and produce stable p99 < 500ms.

Relevant logs & metrics (excerpts):
- grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/lexidocs/d/perf/continuous-batching?from=now-2h&to=now
- Sample serving-runtime log lines:
  [2026-03-10T14:22:31Z] INFO batcher: created batch id=0x7f3c wait_ms=12 size=8
  [2026-03-10T14:23:14Z] WARN batcher: idle_threshold_adjusted from=15ms to=400ms reason=observed_low_rps
  [2026-03-10T14:23:14Z] WARN batcher: pending_batch_window=420ms size=2
  [2026-03-10T14:23:16Z] ERROR api-gateway: upstream read timeout after 1500ms route=/v1/generate

Temporary workaround applied:
- Increased request-level timeout at gateway from 1500ms -> 3500ms for lexidocs routes (mitigates 504s but increases client-visible waiting).
- Rolled back serving-runtime to 2026.2.28 on one pool for validation; observed improvement in p99 during rollback windows.

Notes:
- Behavior appears correlated with a heuristic that increases the continuous-batcher "idle_threshold" when observed RPS drops; in this workload the heuristic over-adjusts and leaves batcher waiting longer for additional requests.
- Rollback to prior serving-runtime improves tail but we need a targeted fix or config knob.
- Customer requests a timeline for a permanent fix and whether dedicated pools require manual config changes.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: a regression in the batcher idle-threshold heuristic introduced in 2026-03-03 rollout.
What we checked:
- Release notes: a change to adaptive batching heuristics (PR #2107) adjusted idle_threshold dynamic scaling.
- Metrics: increased idle_threshold coincides with low inter-burst RPS; pending_batch_window and idle_wait_ms spike preceding p99 events.
- Node-level: no obvious CPU/GPU saturation; autoscaler not thrashing during observed window.
- Clock skew: slight NTP drift found on one worker (-120ms) but not consistently correlated.

Current hypothesis: adaptive idle_threshold logic uses a moving-average window that underestimates inter-arrival variance for low-burst patterns, causing transient over-increase of idle wait and producing long tail waits and timeouts.
Next steps:
- Reproduce in staging with the exact dedicated pool config and RPS pattern (assigned to Liam).
- Instrument batcher with trace IDs to follow per-request wait lifecycle (temp PR to add debug counters).
- Prepare a config flag to cap idle_threshold at 120ms and test with canary traffic.
- If confirmed, prepare hotfix revert or config change to be rolled to lexidocs pool only and then broader rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 — Support (Aisha): Opened on behalf of LexiDocs after customer reported ~3% 504s during morning release window. Customer provided prometheus snapshots and a short request trace. Assigned to SRE for triage.

2026-03-10 16:10 — SRE (Liam): I can reproduce a p99 spike in staging with the described burst pattern. Observed batcher idle_threshold jumping from ~15ms -> 300-400ms after low RPS intervals. Creating a debug deployment to instrument batch wait lifecycle. (Slack: #support, thread: https://slack.redwood/archives/C0123ABCD)

2026-03-11 09:40 — Eng (Priya, serving-runtime): PR #2107 changed adaptive heuristics; adding notes. We will test a cap on idle_threshold and add a safety lower weight on the moving-average to prevent overshoot. Preparing PR for review.
2026-03-11 14:25 — Support (Aisha): LexiDocs accepted temporary gateway timeout increase. They requested that any fix be deployable to their dedicated pool without full platform rollout.

2026-03-12 10:05 — SRE (Liam): Deployed canary with idle_threshold_cap=120ms to one lexidocs node. Early results: p99 reduced to ~420ms under same synthetic workload. Will run 24h canary and prepare rollback plan if no regressions.
2026-03-12 18:30 — Customer (LexiDocs, Helena): Appreciate quick mitigation. Please keep us updated on permanent fix timeline and whether config will require downtime.
resolution: Mitigation: gateway timeout increased and canary config cap applied to one node. Pending permanent fix after validation of PR to cap idle_threshold and adjust moving-average params.
